hotspots.description: Donated by international film star Jackie Chan, the collection of these 400 year-old structures stand regally on the SUTD campus. The buildings were reassembled from about 4,000 pieces and are now used as event and recreational spaces at SUTD.

hotspots.name: chinatown
hotspots.title: For over a decade, SUTDents have designed the CNY light up at Chinatown
hotspots.description: The annual Chinese New Year light-up at Chinatown has become a much-anticipated festival highlight. Each year, the precinct is adorned with hundreds of lanterns designed in collaboration with SUTD undergraduates. In 2022, the Year of the Tiger is the 11th year of SUTD’s participation in the 880 metre-long display.

hotspots.name: campus1
hotspots.title: SUTD Time Capsule
hotspots.description: The SUTD Time Capsule preserves and exhibits the university’s most significant innovations and milestones over the first 10 years. The form of the capsule represents the cyclical nature of time: a periodic surface peels from the ground in an oscillating motion, holding the collection in a secure yet open space. To create this unique form, digital tools and advanced manufacturing methods were developed and applied. The capsule’s surface consists of 3,582 unique panels, which were computationally designed and 3D printed with biopolymers, producing zero waste.

hotspots.name: campus2
hotspots.title: What Design means at SUTD
hotspots.description: Design is the creation of human-centred solutions that better the world. Nurturing Design innovators is crucial to the continued advancement of humankind in a world bombarded by unprecedented challenges. They will transform our lives, drive innovation and grow economies sustainably. At SUTD, our mission is to nurture the future generation of Design innovators.

hotspots.name: spot_fcp
hotspots.title: About the Asia & Pacfic O-RAN Testing and Integration entre (OTIC)
hotspots.description: The world today is highly dependent on the telecommunication infrastructure. This makes it critical to ensure that it is secure, robust and reliable. The new Asia & Pacific OTIC in Singapore will look to advance Singapore’s digital infrastructure capabilities and enable the next level of innovation in future communications and capabilities.

hotspots.name: spot_5g
hotspots.title: 5G drone via VR headset
hotspots.description: The pilot (indoor) controls a 5G-native drone that flies in the AerialArena @ SUTD (outdoor). Two pilots control 5G drones in a virtual environment through VR headsets to compete each other and fly their drones through virtual challenges (e.g., achieve gaming scores if flying through without collision). The winner is the one who brings the drone to the finish line early with the highest score.

hotspots.name: spot_scas
hotspots.title: SCAS Test
hotspots.description: In order to obtain the O-RAN E2E Badge, a gNB must pass the "gNB Security Assurance Specification (SCAS) required by 3GPP SA3". We particularly use gNB from QCT as the System Under Test (SUT) and wrapped around by emulated UE and emulated 5G core. This demo shows the capability of running SCAS test cases automatically with Keysight's Test Management Center (TMC), which can automatically controls emulated UE and 5G core to execute all SCAS test cases, evaluate their results, and obtain reproducible results.

hotspots.name: spot_ocloud
hotspots.title: O-Cloud Test
hotspots.description: To verify that a noisy neighbor DoS attack against O-Cloud for resource starvation will not degrade service availability or performance of the O-RAN system served by the network slice under test. We evaluate the end-to-end performance of 5G users with 2 scenarios: (i) without any noisy neighbor attack as a baseline, and (ii) with noisy neighbor attack trying to exhaust O-Cloud resources.

hotspots.name: spot_radio
hotspots.title: Remote Radio Unit (RRU)
hotspots.description: An indoor RRU (N78 band) provides 5G signal covered the demo area. It is connected through single-mode fibre to the indoor fronthaul gateway (FHGW), indoor BBU and 5G core located in FCCLab's server room.

hotspots.name: spot_safety
hotspots.title: Safety AI
hotspots.description: 5G camera stream video with low-latency and high quality to GPU edge server for processing, and work with the robot arms in the loop to create a virtual fence surrounding the robot-arm. Besides the 5G camera, we also introduce mmWave radar sensor to detect human, which shows potential of combining communication and sensing with mmWave in the future 6G.

hotspots.name: spot_mobile
hotspots.title: 5G Autonomous Mobile Robot
hotspots.description: 5G Autonomous Mobile Robot: 5G smart Autonomous Mobile Robot (5G-AMR) developed by FCP and AI-Mega Centre transmits high quality video via a private 5G networks, and is controlled by a remote operator if needed. The 5G-AMR can autonomously do patrol in a predefined path, and suspicious inspection by offloading AI inference tasks to an edge server, resulting in the reduction of device cost and energy consumption of the 5G-AMR. Whenever detecting a suspicious item or emergency situation, an operator in the central control room will take over the 5G-robot to handle the emergency situation.

hotspots.name: spot_mixed
hotspots.title: Mixed-reality for cabling server rack demo
hotspots.description: This demonstration is designed to showcase the potential of on-site training for new workers through the use of Mixed-Reality (MR) technology. In contrast to traditional training methods that take place in a classroom setting, MR offers a more intuitive and immersive training experience directly at the job site. The integration of 5G technology plays a crucial role by enabling a seamless experience for a multitude of users simultaneously, ensuring low latency and delivering a high-quality and highly engaging training environment.

hotspots.name: spot_ocloud

hotspots.description: To verify that a noisy neighbor DoS attack against O-Cloud for resource starvation will not degrade service availability or performance of the O-RAN system served by the network slice under test. We evaluate the end-to-end performance of 5G users with 2 scenarios: (i) without any noisy neighbor attack as a baseline, and (ii) with noisy neighbor attack trying to exhaust O-Cloud resources.

hotspots.name: spot_planning
hotspots.title: Interactive Planning under Uncertainty
hotspots.description: In this project, we present an interactive behavior planner that considers road context, short-term driver intent, and long-term driving style to predict neighboring vehicle states. We assess its robustness in challenging scenarios with irrational drivers using simulations and a full-size self-driving car. Our experiments demonstrate that our algorithm enhances safety and travel time efficiency in autonomous driving, outperforming baselines even in adversarial scenarios.

hotspots.name: spot_astralis
hotspots.title: ASTRALIS
hotspots.description: In this project we aim to develop tools for heterogeneous robots and human-robot teaming for search and rescue missions. Specifically, the aerial drones can cooperatively follow as well as lead human ground operators during search and rescue missions. The search and rescue scenarios can be generated with high-fidelity with sim-to-real features developed in our simulation environment.

hotspots.description: In this project, we focus on the problem of marine environment monitoring using design principles from bio-inspired swarming and multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL).
